summary: The note tier's create path: a new Dreamer adaptor proposes full notes from a room's conversation, with a deterministic gate deciding create/update/refuse. Ships disabled.
details: design/dreamer-agent-loop/33-note-dreamer-schedule.md §4, issue #98. `NoteCandidateAdaptor` (`nora.language.note_candidates`) mirrors the fact tier's Phase A shape: scope-keyed, watermarked, tool-free, reading one room's message batch plus the workspace's standing note index and proposing `(title, description, body, anchor_date, closing_condition, message_ids)` — never writing a note directly.

note_candidate gains a `kind` column (`miss` | `create`, migration 0049): existing rows are untouched miss-cache rows; a `kind='create'` row is a full staged proposal with its own status lifecycle (`pending` -> `created`/`refused`). Two separate uniqueness domains: the existing `(workspace, probe)` miss key is unchanged, and a new partial unique index, `note_candidate_create_anchor_key` on `(workspace, anchor_date, anchor_entity_ids)` scoped to `kind='create'`, dedupes create-candidates by the note tier's own anchor key rather than by title.

The gate is plain code: it computes the candidate's anchor key and checks it against the workspace's standing notes. A match becomes an update proposal (only if the new body adds something the existing note's head lacks); no match becomes a new note, materialized through the same `DreamSink.propose` verb the tag path's future create tool would use.

Wired under a third, independently-gated flag, `[notes] candidates_enabled` (default false) — mirroring `curator_enabled`'s own two-risks argument: an operator who turned `[notes]` on for the index did not thereby sign up for a background process creating notes on her behalf. Scheduled hourly via the existing per-adaptor `AdaptorSchedule` mechanism (unchanged from the fact tier's own wiring).
limitations: Entity resolution is out of scope (issue #100): a create-candidate's `anchor_entity_ids` is free text, never resolved against `note_entity`, so the gate's anchor-key match always sees an empty entity half and fails closed — every candidate becomes a CREATE, never an UPDATE, until entity resolution lands. This is the identical `no_entity_anchor` limitation the note curator's own merge eligibility already has.

'Adds information' is a syntactic check (is the new body already a substring of the existing note's head, case- and whitespace-insensitively) rather than a semantic one — a paraphrase of an already-tracked arrangement will be misread as new and appended as a revision. This only matters once entity resolution makes the update path reachable.
Ships with `candidates_enabled = false`; no deployed config.toml changes behavior until an operator explicitly turns it on.
